source_window.dataset_title: HM Land Registry plans: title plan (practice guide 40, supplement 5)

field_evidence.title_plan_role: The title plan is one element of a registered title and must be viewed with the register.
field_evidence.general_extent: The title plan provides a graphic representation and identifies the general extent of land in a registered title.
field_evidence.general_boundaries: All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
field_evidence.canonical_extent_limitation: A generic title plan does not by itself establish exact legal-boundary geometry suitable for canonical parcel assertion without target-specific register/plan context.

first_missing_criterion: Verified BUILDING_PRESENT canonical parcel geometry/bbox for this producer. HM Land Registry's official title-plan guidance states that a title plan identifies the general extent of the registered title and normally shows general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002. No target-specific determined-boundary/title-plan/register package is present in the verified lineage. Local OpenCode must retrieve and spatially bind the target-specific title/register/plan context before any canonical parcel bbox is asserted; after that, bind one exact official DEM/LIDAR tile or metadata-index record to the resulting bbox.
exact_blocker: The official HM Land Registry title-plan guidance is directly readable without login and materially changes the method from INSPIRE semantics to title-plan/general-boundary semantics. It confirms that ordinary title plans identify general extent and normally use general boundaries rather than exact legal-boundary coordinates. Therefore this producer cannot promote a generic title-plan extent to canonical parcel geometry without target-specific register/plan context and, where precision is required, determined-boundary evidence. Spatial retrieval/join/materialization remains local OpenCode work.
